answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit bids or claim rewards. A bridge contract records the stake and links each action to one key; when a verifier proves duplicate identities coordinated to claim the same task, the protocol burns their bonds and redistributes the value. A pulse of fresh challenges can make collusion easier to detect, while a lagoon of isolated accounts offers no exemption: each still needs capital. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them multiplies the attacker’s locked funds and potential losses.
